title: 猴哥，还我包！
setting: Mount Emei, Sichuan, the stone steps through the monkey zone, 2 pm.

ranger.name: 管理员
ranger.en: a ranger with a bamboo pole

seller.name: 卖香蕉的阿姨
seller.en: a woman with a basket of bananas

steps.narr: A monkey snatched your bag. Passport, phone: all inside. 🐒
steps.zh: 猴子一把抢走了你的包，护照手机全在里面！

say.en: Shout at the monkey: give me back my bag!
say.tip: 把 + thing + 还给我 = give (it) back to me. 还 huán = return; the same character read hái means 'still'.

mistakes.note: 借 is borrow or lend. Giving something back is 还 huán: 还给我.

ok.narr: The monkey pulls out your sunglasses and puts them on. They suit it. 🕶️
ok.zh: 猴子从包里掏出你的墨镜，戴上了。

miss.narr: It climbs higher, bag and all.
miss.zh: 猴子带着包，爬得更高了。

4.en: Talk the monkey round: let's be reasonable, and the bag comes back first!
answers: 猴哥，有话好好说，先把包还给我！
有话好好说，把包还给我！
猴哥，有话好商量，把包还我！
咱们有话好好说，你先把包还我！
4.gloss: Brother Monkey, let's be reasonable. Give me my bag back first!
4.tip: 有话好好说 = let's talk this over calmly: how you calm anyone down, monkeys included. 先把包还给我 = give me the bag back first.

steps.narr: A ranger with a bamboo pole is strolling down the steps, in no hurry at all.
steps.zh: 一个拿竹竿的管理员慢悠悠地走了过来。

say.en: Get the ranger's help: the monkey snatched your bag!
answers: 师傅，帮帮忙！猴子抢了我的包！
师傅，帮个忙，猴子把我包抢了！
say.gloss: Help me out! The monkey snatched my bag!
say.tip: 帮帮忙 = please, help me out! (帮个忙 is the calmer way to ask.) 抢 qiǎng = snatch: 猴子抢了我的包 = the monkey snatched my bag.

mistakes.note: 偷 tōu is stealing on the sly. Grabbed off your shoulder is 抢 qiǎng.

ok.zh: 那是猴王，我也惹不起它。
ok.en: That's the monkey king. Even I don't mess with him.

miss.zh: 被抢了？这儿天天有，习惯就好。
miss.en: Robbed? Happens every day here. You get used to it.

2.gloss: Help! I've been mugged by a monkey!
2.tip: 被 bèi says who did it to you: 我被猴子抢了 = I've been robbed by a monkey. 帮帮忙 = please, help me out!

4.en: Get the ranger moving: isn't this his job?
answers: 师傅，您不是管理员吗？快帮帮忙！
您不是管这儿的吗？快帮帮我！
管理员！猴子抢了我的包，您快管管啊！
师傅，您是管理员，快帮帮忙吧！
4.gloss: You're the ranger, aren't you? Help me out!
4.tip: 您不是……吗？ = aren't you…?: a question that's really a nudge. 管理员 guǎnlǐyuán = the one in charge here; 管 = to deal with it.

steps.zh: 香蕉！换包专用香蕉！一根五十！
steps.en: Bananas! Get-your-bag-back bananas! Fifty yuan each!

say.en: Fifty yuan for one banana?! Let her know what you think of that.
answers: 一根香蕉五十？你抢钱啊！
say.gloss: Fifty for one banana? Are you robbing me?
say.tip: 你抢钱啊 = 'are you robbing me?', the classic reply to a mad price. 便宜点儿 piányi diǎnr = a bit cheaper.

mistakes.note: Long thin things take 根 gēn: 一根香蕉, 一根筷子.

alts.en: Or: skip her and offer the monkey your sandwich
answers: 猴哥，我拿三明治跟你换！
alts.gloss: Brother Monkey, I'll trade you my sandwich!

then.narr: The monkey sniffs the sandwich, flicks it off the mountain, and goes back to your bag.
then.zh: 猴子闻了闻三明治，随手扔下了山。
我们这儿的猴子，只吃我的香蕉。
then.en: The monkeys round here only eat my bananas.

ok.zh: 不贵不贵！你看，它都开始翻你的护照了！
ok.en: Not dear at all! Look, it's started on your passport!

fail.zh: 嫌贵？那你自己跟猴子谈。
fail.en: Too pricey? Then go and bargain with the monkey yourself.

2.en: Fifty yuan for one banana?! Tell her it's far too dear.
2.gloss: That's far too much! Knock a bit off!
2.tip: 太贵了 = too expensive. 便宜点儿 piányi diǎnr = (make it) a bit cheaper: how every haggle starts.

4.en: Fifty yuan for one banana?! Ask her if this isn't daylight robbery.
answers: 一根香蕉五十？你这不是抢钱吗！
一根五十？这不是抢钱吗！
这么贵，你这不是抢钱吗？
五十块一根，这不就是抢钱吗！
4.gloss: Fifty for one banana? Isn't that daylight robbery?
4.tip: 你这不是……吗？ = isn't this…?: a question that's really an accusation. 抢钱 qiǎng qián = robbery, which any mad price is.

steps.en: Prices just went up. A hundred now.

say.en: Call her bluff. Fine then: you don't want it.
say.tip: 那我不要了 = then I don't want it: the walk-away. The 了 says you've just changed your mind. Then turn, and wait to be called back.

mistakes.note: 没要 means you didn't take it. The walk-away is 不要了: you've decided against it.

ok.zh: 哎哎哎，回来回来！十块，拿去！
ok.en: Hey hey hey, come back! Ten yuan, take it!

fail.en: Suit yourself. A hundred and fifty!

miss.zh: 两百！再不买，护照就被吃了。
miss.en: Two hundred! Any longer and it eats your passport.
You pay ¥200 for one banana. Your passport comes back with a bite out of it. 🛂
miss.zh: 一根香蕉两百块，护照还被咬了一口。

4.en: Call her bluff: you don't want it, and if it comes to that, the bag can go too.
answers: 那我不要了，大不了包也不要了！
不买了！大不了不要这个包了！
算了，不要了，大不了让猴子留着！
那我不要了，大不了再买个包！
4.gloss: Then I don't want it. Worst case, I'll write off the bag too!
4.tip: 大不了 dàbuliǎo = at worst, so what: the word that calls any bluff. 那我不要了 = then I don't want it.

steps.narr: Banana in hand, you edge towards the railing. The monkey lowers your passport. Negotiations begin.
steps.zh: 你拿着香蕉走过去，猴子放下了你的护照。

say.en: Set the terms: banana in one hand, bag in the other.
say.gloss: The banana for the bag, at the same time!
say.tip: 一手交钱，一手交货 = money in one hand, goods in the other: the rule of every fair swap. Swap in 香蕉 and 包.

ok.narr: The monkey drops your bag, grabs the banana, and scampers straight back to the banana seller. It hands her the banana.
ok.zh: 猴子扔下包，抓起香蕉，跑回去交给了阿姨。

miss.narr: The monkey snatches the banana and tosses your bag back. No thanks to you.
miss.zh: 猴子一把抢过香蕉，把包扔了回来。

2.en: Set the terms: the banana for your bag.
2.gloss: Banana for you, bag back to me!
2.tip: A给你，B还我 = A for you, B back to me: a swap in two short clauses. 还 huán = give back.

4.en: Set the terms: banana in one hand, bag in the other, and the monkey won't lose out.
answers: 一手交香蕉，一手交包，你不吃亏！
猴哥，香蕉换包，你又不吃亏！
香蕉给你，包还我，谁也不吃亏！
拿包换香蕉，这买卖你不吃亏！
4.gloss: Banana in one hand, bag in the other. You won't lose out!
4.tip: 你不吃亏 = you won't lose out: the line that closes a deal. 一手交钱，一手交货 = money in one hand, goods in the other.

steps.zh: 这根香蕉，今天卖了八回了。
steps.en: That banana's been sold eight times today.
Bag: back. Passport: slightly chewed. The banana: already back on sale.
steps.zh: 包拿回来了。那根香蕉，又回到了阿姨的篮子里。
